fixes.explanation: David is the king (2 Samuel 5:3), but that's not the reason he gives here. Verse 5 says, “…for You are the God of my salvation…” Notice he doesn't bring up his title at all. When he asks to be taught, he comes as someone who needs the LORD, not as the one in charge.
Yes, friend. Verse 5 says, “all day long I wait for You.” That's the whole day spent waiting. I'd be checking my oven timer every two minutes.

A year would be some serious waiting. But verse 5 says, “all day long I wait for You.” The word is day, so the waiting fills his whole day. I think that makes it sound like something you could actually do.
It's true, actually. Verse 9 says, “He guides the humble in what is right and teaches them His way.” Guided AND taught, so the LORD does both. I'd say that's a great deal for the humble.
That's it. Verse 10 says, “All the LORD’s ways are loving and faithful to those who keep His covenant and His decrees.” Loving AND faithful, both at once. And David tells you exactly who gets them.
Yes! Verse 12 says, “Who is the man who fears the LORD? He will instruct him in the path chosen for him.” So the LORD does the teaching, and there's a path chosen for that man.
David is a king (2 Samuel 5:3), so it's an easy guess, but verse 12 doesn't say this. It says the LORD “…will instruct him in the path chosen for him.” The promise there is instruction, not a throne.

That's the word. Verse 13 says, “His soul will dwell in prosperity, and his descendants will inherit the land.” So it reaches past the man himself, on to his descendants. That's a blessing with a long line behind it.
That's backwards, friend. Verse 19 says, “Consider my enemies, for they are many, and they hate me with vicious hatred.” Many, not few. David brings it straight to the LORD.

Yes, friend. Verse 21 says, “May integrity and uprightness preserve me, because I wait for You.” He asks for integrity and uprightness to preserve him, and he gives his waiting on the LORD as the reason. Waiting and integrity in one breath, and I bet that's not easy to hold together.
